why: I compared each check's PASS/FAIL against its expect line. Checks 1–4 ask only for exact output plus a newline, using cmp, and Check 1 also asks for exit 0. Check 5 asks only for exact output with JSON backslash-t escapes. Its first printf actually writes two backslashes, but the brief tells the verifier to confirm the expected file and fix it, so this doesn't make the condition stricter. Check 6 asks for "exit=0" and at least one test that runs bin/csv2json.js with --tsv on tab-containing input and asserts on its output. That matches the line's words and doesn't ask for the test:cli script. Check 7 asks only that README describe --tsv and include an example that uses it. The proof's stricter README form ("node bin/csv2json.js --tsv < file"), the test:cli note, the mutation test, the flag-position check and the parse.js check all sit under "Advisory". No PASS/FAIL condition goes beyond what the words require.
